Category: Nonblocking Waveform Update Execution
Requirement Statement: The firmware shall avoid blocking delays that prevent normal firmware execution during duty-cycle updates.
Source Text / Evidence:
Avoid blocking delays that prevent normal firmware execution; duty-cycle updates should be 
timer/tick driven.
Acceptance Criteria: Code review shows no long blocking loops or delays in the update path; updates are performed by timer/tick or an equivalent non-blocking mechanism.
Failure Behavior: If blocking occurs, the ramp may jitter or stall; firmware shall log the condition if logging exists (not specified).
Resource Impact: Requires use of timers/interrupts or RTOS tick; minimal CPU overhead per update.
Comments / Open Questions: "Normal firmware execution" and the maximum acceptable blocking time are not defined. The note suggests timer/tick-driven updates but does not mandate a specific mechanism.

Category: Nonblocking Waveform Update Execution
Requirement Statement: Duty-cycle increment steps shall be sufficiently small to produce a smooth ramp without perceptible jumps or long pauses.
Source Text / Evidence:
Use sufficiently small duty-cycle increments to create a smooth ramp. A target implementation is

Acceptance Criteria: Observed ramp on oscilloscope shows no unexpected jumps or long pauses; step size is small enough that samples at 2.5 s and 7.5 s read approximately 50%.
Parameters / Constraints: Duty-cycle increment step and update interval
Failure Behavior: Large steps or pauses will cause visible or measurable discontinuities in the ramp.
Resource Impact: Higher update rates increase CPU/interrupt load.
Comments / Open Questions: No quantitative maximum for step size or update interval is specified. The document gives a target of 1% every 50 ms but does not make it mandatory.

Category: PWM Timer and PA8 Output Driver
Requirement Statement: The D7/PA8 output shall remain in a defined inactive state with no pulses until PWM is fully configured and enabled, and the first active duty cycle shall be 0%.
Source Text / Evidence: Start PWM generation automatically after board initialization. Begin each cycle at 0% duty cycle.
Inference Rationale: Without an explicit glitch-free startup requirement, PA8 may briefly toggle during clock/peripheral configuration, violating the requirement to begin at 0% and confusing oscilloscope-based verification.
Acceptance Criteria: On power-up or reset, a capture on D7 shows a constant level with no pulses before PWM enable; the first active PWM period begins at 0% duty cycle.
Preconditions: Power-up or reset; firmware initialization in progress.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: No output toggling occurs until PWM is enabled; first commanded duty cycle is 0%.
Comments / Open Questions: If PWM polarity is configured inverted, confirm which inactive level (high or low) is required during startup.

Category: PWM Ramp Control Logic
Requirement Statement: The firmware shall saturate the computed PWM duty cycle to the inclusive range 0% to 100% before applying it to the output.
Source Text / Evidence: Duty-cycle endpoints: 0% and 100%.
Inference Rationale: Finite step size, arithmetic rounding, or accumulation error can produce values slightly outside [0%,100%], causing wraparound or out-of-range behavior that violates the stated endpoints.
Acceptance Criteria: Across all updates, the measured duty cycle on D7 never exceeds the range [0%,100%]; test injection of out-of-range commands results in 0% or 100% output respectively.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Output duty cycle never overshoots below 0% or above 100%.

Category: PWM Timer and PA8 Output Driver
Requirement Statement: If PWM/timer or PA8 configuration fails during initialization, the firmware shall place PA8 in a defined inactive state and shall not toggle the output.
Source Text / Evidence: Do not connect a high‑power load directly to the MCU pin; use an external driver stage when controlling loads that exceed GPIO electrical limits.
Inference Rationale: The PRD intends safe, low-power observation of PWM. Absent defined failure behavior, partial configuration could drive unintended pulses on PA8, risking hardware misuse and invalid test results.
Acceptance Criteria: With an induced configuration failure (e.g., invalid timer/channel selection during a negative test build), code inspection shows the error path leaves PA8 inactive; measurement confirms no toggling on D7.
Preconditions: Initialization detects a PWM/timer or pin configuration error.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: PA8 remains in a stable inactive state; no PWM waveform is produced.
Failure Behavior: Remain inactive and report failure through build/test logs if available; do not attempt to drive PA8.
Comments / Open Questions: Define how configuration failures are detected and what constitutes an error in this context.

Category: PWM Timer and PA8 Output Driver
Requirement Statement: PWM duty-cycle percentage shall be defined as the proportion of time that D7/PA8 is at logic-high level within each PWM period.
Source Text / Evidence: The D7 pin is a 3.3 V MCU logic output. The requirement refers to PWM duty cycle/effective output, not a variable 5 V supply rail.
Inference Rationale: Verification of 0%, 50%, and 100% duty cycles requires an unambiguous polarity definition; without it, measurements on D7 may be interpreted inconsistently across tools or configurations.
Acceptance Criteria: At a commanded 50% duty, the measured high-time on D7 is approximately 50% of the PWM period; at 0% the pin is low continuously; at 100% the pin is high continuously.
Comments / Open Questions: Confirm whether any use case requires inverted polarity (active-low PWM).

Category: PWM Ramp Control Logic
Requirement Statement: At both duty-cycle endpoints (0% and 100%), the firmware shall reverse the ramp direction immediately with no intentional hold time.
Source Text / Evidence: Immediately reverse the ramp direction at 100% duty cycle.; Ramp shape: linear with no intentional hold time at 0% or 100%.
Acceptance Criteria: Oscilloscope/logic-analyzer capture shows no plateau at either 0% or 100% beyond the update interval; the ramp direction reverses immediately at both endpoints. Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Ramp direction reverses immediately at both endpoints; no intentional dwell is observable.
Comments / Open Questions: No maximum allowable endpoint dwell time is specified.
